text: Hurstwood leaned forward. The whole audience was silent and intent. "Let the woman you look upon be wise or vain," said Carrie, her eyes bent sadly upon the lover, who had sunk into a seat, "beautiful or homely, rich or poor, she has but one thing she can really give or refuse--her heart." Drouet felt a scratch in his throat. "Her beauty, her wit, her accomplishments, she may sell to you; but her love is the treasure without money and without price."
